requirementname: Print View The application shall provide functionality to print the current view. Allow user to initiate printing Support different printing methods based on operating environment The application should display a print dialog before initiating the print process. The application should handle both Java2D and Quartz rendering engines for printing.

Create and manage connections between figures The system shall allow users to create and manage connections (lines) between figures on the drawing canvas. Allow creation of new connections between selected figures Determine valid connection targets based on figure properties and position Update connection endpoints when dragging a handle Users should be able to initiate a connection from any figure and select a target figure. The system must validate that the selected target is connectable before establishing a connection. Connections can be updated dynamically as the user drags one of its handles.

Delete Figures The user can delete selected figures from the drawing canvas. Select figures Remove selected figures When a figure is selected and the 'delete' action is performed, all selected figures are removed from the drawing canvas. If any of the selected figures cannot be removed (e.g., due to constraints), an audible alert is provided and no figures are deleted.

Delete Connections The user can remove existing connections between objects in the drawing. Remove connection handles Update related figures When a connection is deleted, all associated connection handles are removed from the view. Any dependent figures or nodes that are no longer connected should be updated to reflect the removal of the connection.

Select and Deselect Figures The user should be able to select or deselect figures in the drawing area. Allow selection of figures Allow deselection of figures When a figure is selected, its state should reflect that it is selected (e.g., highlighted). When a figure is deselected, its state should revert to the unselected state. The selection state of a figure can be toggled by user interaction.

User can manipulate figures by rotating, scaling, or moving them The user should be able to rotate, scale, and move figures within the drawing canvas. Support for rotating figures around a center point Ability to scale (resize) figures Option to move (translate) figures Users can initiate rotation, scaling, or moving of any figure by interacting with the appropriate handles. Rotations should be performed around a defined center point for composite figures. Scaling and moving operations should update the figure's position and size accurately on the canvas.

Change properties of color sliders The user can modify the properties of color sliders in the application. Allow modification of color slider properties Update visual representation of color sliders based on property changes Users should be able to change the appearance and behavior of color sliders through a graphical interface Changes made by users should trigger appropriate updates in the application's UI

Edit Text in Figures Users can edit text within figures displayed on the drawing canvas. Allow users to modify text attributes Support text editing for various figure types The system should enable users to select and edit text content within any figure that contains text. Editing text should update the corresponding attribute values in the figure's data model.

Align Bezier Control Points The user can align control points on a Bezier curve to maintain symmetry or other geometric properties. Allow adjustment of control point positions Maintain colinearity between control points When the user modifies one control point, the corresponding opposite control point is adjusted to maintain colinearity if the shift key is pressed. The system updates the Bezier curve nodes and invalidates the area affected by the change.

Change Z-ordering of Drawing Elements The user can change the z-ordering of drawing elements to control their stacking order in the view. Bring figure to front Send figure to back Users should be able to bring a selected figure to the front or send it to the back without affecting other figures' positions. The z-ordering change should trigger an area invalidation event for the affected drawing area.

Action Management The system shall allow users to group and ungroup actions related to figures. Group actions Ungroup actions Users can create groups of actions for figure manipulation tasks. Users can ungroup actions to separate them into individual actions.

Launch the Application When the application is launched, it initializes the view and displays it to the user. Initialize the application Create and display a view The application should initialize its preferences based on the model or class. The application should create and initialize a view for displaying content. The application should show the created view to the user.

Open an existing drawing As a user, I want to open an existing drawing file so that I can continue working on it. Display the last used project Allow selection of recent files The system should display a list of recently opened files. The system should allow the user to select and open any of these files.

Save a Drawing The user can save the current drawing to a file. Provide an option to save the drawing Store the saved file path When the 'Save' action is invoked, a file chooser dialog appears allowing the user to select a location and filename for saving the drawing. The system updates the preferences with the last used file path when a drawing is saved. If there are unsaved changes, the system prompts the user before saving.

Large Drawings The system must support the creation and display of drawings that can be as large as needed without performance degradation. Support for large drawings Efficient rendering of large figures Drawings should not degrade in performance when their size exceeds typical user expectations The system should allow users to zoom into and out of large drawings without significant lag or memory issues

Redraw Figures Quickly Ensure that figures are redrawn efficiently when modified. Efficient figure redrawing Quick response to figure changes Figures should be updated within a short time frame after modification. The system should maintain performance even with a large number of figures.

Quickly Locate Figures Based on Coordinates The system must efficiently locate figures based on their x-y coordinates. Support for coordinate-based figure location Use of spatial data structures for efficient querying The system should be able to quickly find a figure within a given bounding box using the `findFiguresWithin` method in `QuadTreeDrawing`. The system should use a quadtree structure to optimize the search process, as evidenced by the implementation of `findFiguresWithin`.

Clipboard Operations The system shall support copying, cutting, and pasting graphical elements via the clipboard. Support for copying graphical elements to the clipboard Support for cutting graphical elements to the clipboard Support for pasting graphical elements from the clipboard When a user selects 'Copy' or 'Cut', the selected graphical element(s) shall be copied to the system's clipboard. When a user selects 'Paste', the contents of the system's clipboard shall be pasted as new graphical elements at the current cursor position. The system shall handle image data formats when reading from and writing to the clipboard.

Support macOS-specific user interface Ensure the application provides a macOS-native look and feel, including menu bar integration. Integrate with macOS menu bar Use Quaqua Look and Feel for macOS The application's main window should have an integrated menu bar when running on macOS. The application should use the Quaqua Look and Feel to match macOS visual design standards.

Short Startup Time Ensure the system initializes quickly to provide a responsive user experience. System initialization User responsiveness The application should initialize within 2 seconds on average. The main window and initial views should be displayed within 1 second.

Periodic Auto-Save The system should automatically save the current drawing state at regular intervals to prevent data loss. Automatically save the drawing state Save state at regular intervals The application saves the drawing state when changes are made and within a specified interval. Saved states can be recovered if the application crashes or is closed unexpectedly.
